# Sample size planning - scope B 

## Data-generating model

### Data-generating distribution

Bernoulli & Binomial (cf. @sec-scope-cd).

### Planning for precision (Bayesian approach)

Beta-binomial model:

- prior: $\psi_{t=t'} \sim Beta(\alpha, \beta)$
- likelihood: $nobs_{t=t'}|\psi_{t=t'} \sim Binom(\psi_{t=t'}, I)$
- posterior: $\psi_{t=t'}|nobs_{t=t'} \sim Beta(k + \alpha, n - k + \beta)$
  - with: x: number of successes, n: number of trials
  
Prior set to uninformative / flat: $Beta(1, 1)$
Posterior: $Beta(k + 1, n - k + 1)$

$1-\alpha$ quantile of the posterior beta-distribution to get upper bound of credible interval.

Given zero-sightings only:

- Show upper bound as a function of sample size.
- Provide function to numerically find sample size for which interval (just) has desired width.

<!--quantile function: inverted cdf
if a and b are positive integers: 
cdf of binmial with specific parameterization can be used
(see: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beta_distribution)-->

#| include: false

alpha = 0.1
n = 100

qbeta(
  p = alpha,
  shape1 = 1,
  shape2 = n + 1,
  ncp = 0,
  lower.tail = FALSE,
  log.p = FALSE
)
